acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-01 — Terraform provisions, per environment, an API Gateway REST API with a REGIONAL endpoint type, integrated with a Lambda (nodejs24.x, not VPC-attached, no Lambda layer) whose IAM role grants only s3:PutObject on the event bucket ARN and ssm:GetParameter on the webhook-secret parameter ARN. The parameter is a SecureString encrypted with the AWS-managed key alias/aws/ssm, whose key policy already permits decryption by account principals via kms:ViaService — so no separate kms:Decrypt grant is required. (If a customer-managed key is ever adopted, kms:Decrypt must be added scoped to that key's ARN, never Resource = "*".) No wildcard resource ARNs anywhere. The REST API sets disable_execute_api_endpoint = true, so the custom domain is the only route in. This restores and reduces the inherited apiGateway.tf, which is already a REST API, rather than authoring a new aws_apigatewayv2_* stack.

verification.definingInputProperty: A planned REST API (v1) in each environment root, restored from future-state rather than newly authored as apigatewayv2
verification.assertions: aws_api_gateway_rest_api is present with endpoint_configuration REGIONAL; no aws_apigatewayv2_* resource exists; the Lambda has no vpc_config and no layers reference

verification.definingInputProperty: Every IAM policy document in the module
verification.assertions: No wildcard resource ARN anywhere — the negative half of least-privilege
disable_execute_api_endpoint is true; and no kms:Decrypt statement appears in the role policy, since the parameter uses the AWS-managed alias/aws/ssm key

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-02 — An AWS WAF Web ACL is attached directly to the REST API stage via aws_wafv2_web_acl_association, with scope = "REGIONAL" in the API's own region (us-west-2) — no CloudFront distribution is involved. It carries the aws.md managed rule set — AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet, AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet, AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList — plus an explicit rate-limit rule. WAF logging is enabled to an S3 destination with a 60-day expiry per aws.md.

verification.definingInputProperty: A deployed REGIONAL Web ACL associated to the REST API stage, receiving real requests
verification.assertions: get-web-acl shows all four rules and scope REGIONAL; the association targets the stage ARN; a probe request matching a managed rule returns 403; a benign request is NOT blocked; the WAF log bucket receives a record and carries a 60-day expiry rule
No CloudFront distribution and no CLOUDFRONT-scope Web ACL — the design uses native REST-API association

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-03 — The custom domain is the only route to the API, and every request through it traverses the WAF. Two independently-checked halves: 1. No second route. With disable_execute_api_endpoint = true, a request to the default https://{api-id}.execute-api.{region}.amazonaws.com/... hostname returns 403. Without that attribute the default hostname stays live, so this is asserted explicitly rather than assumed. 2. The WAF is in the path. A request to the custom domain matching a managed rule is blocked with 403 before reaching the Lambda, evidenced by the absence of a corresponding Lambda invocation in that window; a benign request reaches the Lambda and returns 404 from the empty registry. Because WAF attaches natively to the stage, no origin-verify header mechanism is required.

verification.definingInputProperty: Three requests: one to the default execute-api hostname, one to the custom domain matching a managed rule, and a benign control to the custom domain
verification.assertions: The execute-api request returns 403 (default endpoint disabled); the rule-matching request returns 403 AND produces no Lambda invocation in that window; the benign request reaches the Lambda and returns 404 from the empty registry

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-04 — A per-environment custom hostname resolves and serves the endpoint: hooks.dev.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com and hooks.prod.personal-events.fifthdimensionengineering.com, each backed by a regional ACM certificate in the API's region, DNS-validated in that environment's own zone from AWE-151 — IaC: S3 event bucket & delegated DNS, with the alias A record targeting the API Gateway regional domain name.

verification.definingInputProperty: Public DNS resolution and a real TLS handshake against the regional API Gateway custom domain
verification.assertions: The hostname resolves to the API Gateway regional domain; HTTPS completes with a valid regional certificate; the unregistered path returns 404

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-05 — A generic Lambda handler routes a request to a registered integration by path (e.g. /github), hands it the raw request (headers + raw body), and maps its outcome to an HTTP status. The handler is integration-agnostic: it contains no provider names, no signature verification, and no classification. This story ships the registry empty, so every POST to an unregistered path returns 404; GitHub registers itself in AWE-156 — GitHub webhook handler (signature verify → S3).

verification.definingInputProperty: A stub WebhookIntegration returning each WebhookOutcome variant, plus an unregistered path
verification.assertions: Each outcome maps to its documented status; an unregistered path returns 404
No provider name or signature vocabulary appears — the integration-agnostic half of the criterion

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-06 — Persistence goes through the single existing Repository. The handler and its integrations obtain put from the EventRepository Context.Tag (@personal-events/core, AWE-153 — Core layer contracts), provided by the S3EventRepositoryLayer from @personal-events/s3-repository (AWE-213 — S3 event repository & push CLI). No new S3 write path, no new event-writing package, and no direct @aws-sdk/client-s3 use outside that layer.

verification.definingInputProperty: The whole ingest app and the packages directory
verification.assertions: No S3 SDK import in the app; no event-sink package exists — the static half

verification.definingInputProperty: A handler test providing a capturing EventRepository layer
verification.assertions: put/putAll is invoked through the tag — the behavioural half, which the static check alone cannot establish

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-07 — Raw body integrity is preserved. The handler passes the exact request bytes through to the integration (base64-decoded only when isBase64Encoded is true), never JSON-parsing and re-serialising first, because AWE-156's HMAC signs the exact bytes. A test asserts a body with unusual-but-valid whitespace and Unicode survives byte-identical.

verification.definingInputProperty: A body containing significant whitespace, a trailing newline, multi-byte UTF-8, and key ordering that a re-serialisation round-trip would alter
verification.assertions: The bytes the stub integration receives are identical to the bytes sent, for both base64 and plain encodings

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-08 — Effect throughout: every effectful function returns Effect; pure fallible helpers return Either; a raw Promise appears only in the exported Lambda handler, via Effect.runPromise (per CLAUDE.md).

verification.definingInputProperty: Every source module except the handler export

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-09 — Logging is Effect's Logger, not winston. Every record carries level, env, timestamp (ms), service (webhook-ingest) and the request id from event.requestContext.requestId, emitted as JSONL to the CloudWatch stream per .agents/guidance/logging.md. The webhook secret is never logged, at any level.

verification.definingInputProperty: A sentinel secret value injected, exercised across every failure path in the AC-11 inventory
verification.assertions: The captured log output contains the sentinel zero times; every emitted record is valid JSON carrying level, env, timestamp with ms, service and requestId

verification.definingInputProperty: The whole ingest app including package.json

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-10 — terraform fmt -check, validate and plan are clean for every environment root, and a second plan after apply reports no drift — including no perpetual diff on the WAF Web ACL, the REST API deployment, or the ACM certificate validation.

verification.command: for d in development production; do terraform -chdir=infra/environments/$d plan -detailed-exitcode || exit 1; done
verification.definingInputProperty: A plan executed AFTER a completed apply, across the complete set of environment roots
verification.assertions: -detailed-exitcode returns 0 for every root; no perpetual diff on the Web ACL, the REST API deployment, or the certificate validation

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-11 — Failure modes, each logged with the offending value and mapped to the right status: unroutable path → 404; malformed request body → 400; S3 write failure → 5xx (so the sender can redeliver — GitHub does not auto-retry, making this load-bearing); missing SSM parameter → 5xx with a message naming the parameter; IAM denial → 5xx with the denied action and resource named.

verification.definingInputProperty: The complete enumerated set of 5 handler-reachable failure cases, each carrying the property that triggers its specific mode
verification.assertions: Each case returns its exact documented status and logs the offending value; a guard asserts the table length equals 5. The WAF-blocked 403 is deliberately excluded — it never reaches the handler and is proven live under AC-03, so including it would mean either an over-long table or a fake in-Lambda 403 path

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-12 — Guidance conformance: G-C-P separation across distinct modules, Repository pattern (no SDK above the boundary), Record lookups rather than if/else if on a discriminator, no accumulator loops, no enums, explicit return types. Verified by biome + typecheck.

verification.command: pnpm --filter @personal-events/webhook-ingest exec biome check src && pnpm --filter @personal-events/webhook-ingest typecheck

verification.assertions: No TypeScript enum — a counterexample check biome does not enforce
